core_obligations: Set up the triangulated framework (proof lines 14391-14402): locally constant Lambda-modules of finite type form a weak Serre subcategory, so the complexes whose cohomology sheaves are such form a strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory of D(C, Lambda) by the derived-category criterion.

Compare successive powers (proof lines 14403-14413): the displayed distinguished triangle relates K tensor^L Lambda/I^{n+1} to K tensor^L Lambda/I^n and K tensor^L I^n/I^{n+1}, and the second object is rewritten as (K tensor^L Lambda/I) tensor^L_{Lambda/I} I^n/I^{n+1}.

Conclude the induction (proof lines 14414-14416): the locally-constant tensor product lemma shows that the associated graded piece has locally constant finite type cohomology because K tensor^L Lambda/I does, and the saturatedness of the subcategory then propagates the property from n to n+1, giving the statement for all n.
proof_roadmap: Record the weak Serre and triangulated-subcategory framework for locally constant finite type cohomology.
Use the distinguished triangle comparing I^{n+1}, I^n and the associated graded, rewriting the graded piece as a tensor product over Lambda/I.
Apply the tensor product lemma to identify the graded piece and use saturation to induct on n.
difficulty_reason: The lemma propagates local constancy of the cohomology of K tensor^L Lambda/I to all the powers Lambda/I^n (statement lines 14378-14388). The proof (proof lines 14390-14416) places the property in a saturated triangulated subcategory, uses the distinguished triangle comparing successive powers, rewrites the associated graded piece as a tensor product over Lambda/I, and applies the locally-constant tensor product lemma so that saturation gives the induction. H2: one triangle computation inside a standard framework, written out.
